AyysKing.notes: All eight drum machines share one implementation, src/drum_machine_base.hh. The Length and Speed jacks carry no printing; the manual's opening section says every unlabelled jack is the CV input for the parameter beside it. Two things the manual does not say. The Length knob is configured as a percentage from 0 to 100 (line 74), but line 98 clamps the knob to a floor of 0.1 and line 99 then maps 0.1..1.0 onto 0.19..1.0 of the sample, so fully left plays 19% of the sample, not none of it. And line 141 advances the playback position by the speed ratio alone, with no conversion against the engine sample rate, where the one-shot modules divide by it (one_shot_base.hh:118); an engine at 48kHz therefore plays these samples sharp. The Sum knob scales only the Sum output; individual outputs are set at line 137 before it is applied.

lines: Plays one of sixteen recorded hand clap samples, at a playback speed you set and under a decay envelope
Chooses which of the sixteen samples is played, numbered 1 to 16
Shifts the sample choice, 0.625V moving it by one sample; it is added to the Sample knob and the total held between the first sample and the sixteenth
Sets the playback speed, and with it the pitch: the recorded speed at centre, 0.01 times speed fully left and twice speed fully right
Shifts the playback speed, 5V covering the whole of the Pitch knob's travel; the total of knob and voltage is held inside that travel
Sets an exponential decay over the sample, 5ms fully left and the whole length of the chosen sample fully right
Shifts the decay time, 5V covering the whole of the Decay knob's travel; the total of knob and voltage is held inside that travel
A rising edge past 1V restarts the sample from its beginning
Scales the output level: 0V silences it, 5V gives full level, and anything above 5V counts as 5V
Pressing it restarts the sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever the module is triggered, from the button or from Trig
The chosen sample at the set speed under the decay envelope, a full-scale sample reaching ±10V
Note — no sound comes out until the module is triggered, either by a rising edge at Trig or by a press of the button.
Note — the sample number, and the sample length the Decay knob is scaled against, are read at the moment of the trigger; turning Sample part way through a note does not change what is playing.
Note — with Vol unpatched the level is full, so patching a cable that rests at 0V silences the module.

Clap.notes: All ten acoustic one-shot modules share one implementation, src/one_shot_base.hh, and differ only in which sixteen samples they hold. The Sample, Pitch and Decay jacks carry no printing on the panel; the manual's opening section says every unlabelled jack is the CV input for the parameter beside it. Decay is scaled against the length of the sample that was selected at the trigger, so the same knob position gives a different time on a long sample and a short one. The samples are stored at 44.1kHz and the playback position is rate-converted against the engine sample rate, so the pitch does not move with the engine rate.
